title: The Window Across the Courtyard
body: For three summers I had been careful. Careful with my words, careful with my heart, careful never to want anything I couldn't explain. Then the heat came to Lisbon, and with it, the man across the courtyard. Every evening at nine, his window opened. Every evening, I pretended not to watch. He read with his sleeves rolled, a glass of wine catching the last of the light. Once, he looked up. I didn't look away. Neither did he. I began to dress for that window. A silk slip the colour of wine. My hair down. The lamp turned low, so he could see only what I chose. On the night of the storm, the power failed across the whole street. Candles appeared in windows, one by one. His was the last. He held it up, like a question. I answered it. I crossed the courtyard barefoot, rain on my shoulders, my heart louder than the thunder. He opened the door before I knocked. "I wondered when you'd come," he said. "So did I," I told him. For three summers I had been careful. That night, I was honest. I told him exactly what I wanted, and I watched it land in his eyes. Not surprise. Relief. His hand found the small of my back. Mine found the buttons of his shirt, slowly, one at a time, because I wanted to remember every one. The candle burned down. The rain didn't stop until morning. I don't know his last name. I know the sound he makes when he says mine. Some nights, the bravest thing a woman can do is ask.

packaging.thumbnail_brief: a woman with dark wet hair holding a candle at a rain-streaked window at night, warm candlelight on her face, a man's lit window far behind her
packaging.description: Three summers of being careful. One night of rain, a candle in the window across the courtyard, and a woman who decides to ask. A short cinematic story for adults.

comment_question: Would you have crossed the courtyard?

stills.style: A still frame from an intimate, sensual art-house romance shot on 35mm: photorealistic real adults and real places in Lisbon, warm low-key light from one motivated source (a lamp, a candle, the last sun, dawn through rain), soft shadows, shallow depth of field, rich amber, honey and deep blue tones, fine film grain, anamorphic 16:9 composition. Tender, adult and suggestive, never explicit: everyone stays clothed; closeness is shown by glances, hands, light and shadow.

genre.note: This episode is a sensual, cinematic romantic drama about an adult woman's desire and her decision to ask for it, told tastefully. It is NOT horror: no fear, threat, scares, monsters, dread or darkness for its own sake. Pictures are warm, intimate and suggestive but never explicit: everyone stays clothed; intimacy is shown through glances, hands, candlelight, rain and shadow. The narrator sounds warm, intimate and unhurried, never afraid. Music is tender and romantic, never ominous.

music_prompts.unease: Intimate late-evening film score: warm solo piano, soft sustained strings, a hint of Portuguese guitar, slow, tender and sensual, instrumental, gentle and spacious under a voice
music_prompts.dread: Building romantic tension film score: warm cello and soft piano over a slow pulse, rain-like piano figures, swelling gently with longing, lush but restrained, instrumental

stills.performance_guide: How a warm, intimate narrator sounds: plain, natural speech carries most of the story (leave at least half the sentences ""); [hesitantly] or [curious] early, as she starts to watch; [softly] for tender lines; [whispers] for at most two intimate lines, never twice in a row; one [sighs] or [exhales] where she really would; [quietly] for the last line. Never fearful.
